notes:
The page that shows a grid can be perfectly readable and still have no findable border. Its right-hand rule is printed hard against the black bar the paper runs down the edge of the puzzle, and its left-hand one against the column of horoscope text; the threshold welds all three into one shape 898 pixels wide that is not square and is not the grid. The detector reported two candidates, best score 0.00, on a photograph a person reads without effort.

It is in the corpus because it is the page that forced the locator to stop needing an outline. Its eighty-one cells are perfectly clear - a border can be lost to whatever is printed beside it, a cell cannot, because it is a hole inside the grid - and solving the corners from where those cells are takes it from 0.00 to 0.40 through the ordinary scorer. See CellGrid.

Thirty-one printed digits and fifty written answers, all in the same ballpoint at very nearly the size of the print, on creased newsprint photographed at an angle. Machine-verified like the rest: the complete grid is a valid solution, and the printed digits have exactly one solution, which is that grid. One of the set sent in by another reader.
